clean.description: Ordinary fashion captions and alt text, written natively in the language as community members would write them, without reference to the term lists. Every entry is expected to pass text screening, except entries labelled expected review, which carry one of the policy's deliberate review terms and the reason it is kept.

entries.text: Weather check before getting dressed: 7°C at 8am, 16°C by 2pm, rain after 5. So it's a light merino jumper, a waterproof trench, ankle boots that can handle puddles, and a tote big enough to stash the scarf once the sun comes out. Layers win again.

Long post but I need advice. My best friend's wedding is outdoors in late September and the forecast keeps flipping between 14°C and 24°C. I have a strapless satin midi in sage but I'm worried about getting cold. Wrap, cropped jacket, or just bring a pashmina?

Finally nailed the capsule wardrobe: two pairs of trousers, one pair of jeans, five tops, two knits, a blazer, a trench and a coat. Everything goes with everything, and getting dressed on a rainy Monday takes about four minutes now.

Packing for a week by the sea: two bikinis, one swimsuit, three linen shirts, a slip dress for dinners, thong sandals, white trainers, and a cardigan because evenings on the coast can be surprisingly cool even in July.
Today was one of those days where the weather changed every hour. Started with fog and a heavy coat, ended with sunshine and the coat over my arm. Next time I'm taking the thin quilted jacket.

I used to think bodycon dresses weren't for me. Then I found one in a thick ribbed knit with long sleeves, paired it with chunky boots and a long coat, and it felt cosy and easy. Sometimes it's all about the fabric.
Small styling tip for hot weather: choose loose natural fibres, lighter colours, and keep a thin shirt in your bag for air-conditioned rooms. Your future self in the freezing cinema will thank you.

To everyone who commented on my green coat yesterday: it's secondhand, about twenty years old, and the lining was falling apart until my neighbour helped me replace it. Proof that good tailoring lasts.

My winter commute uniform after years of trial and error: thermal leggings under wide trousers, a merino top, a down jacket that covers my hips, waterproof boots with grippy soles, and mittens. Pretty? Maybe not. Warm? Always.
Spring wardrobe swap done! Packed away the chunky knits and wool coats, washed the cotton dresses, and found a skirt I forgot I owned. Wearing it today with a denim jacket and white trainers.
Question for the petite folks: how do you wear midi skirts without feeling swamped? I'm 155 cm and I've tried heels, but I walk too much for them. Would a pointed flat or a higher waist help?
Wore my late grandfather's tweed cap today with a navy coat. It still smells a little like his shed and I think it suits me. Some pieces are worth so much more than what they cost.
The forecast said 30°C and humid, so I went with a sleeveless linen dress in nude, flat sandals and a woven bag. Hair tied up, sunglasses on, and a little fan in my bag for the tram.
Rate my rainy day outfit: olive parka, grey hoodie, black jeans, black rubber boots and a navy beanie. Not glamorous but I stayed completely dry walking the kids to school.

Lolita fashion meetup in the park this afternoon! Everyone looked amazing. I wore a cream dress with a lace collar, a big bow at the back, white tights and round-toe shoes. The weather was kind to us, 21°C and sunny.

entries.text: Black slip dress for the evening, oversized knit cardigan on top, and ankle boots. When it's 15°C after sunset this is my favourite way to stay comfortable and still look dressed up.
Office dress codes are tricky in a heatwave. Mine today: sleeveless silk top, cropped wide trousers, open-toe mules and a lightweight blazer that stays on the chair until the client call.
Not sure about cropped tops at 40, but I tried a slightly cropped knit with very high-waisted trousers and honestly it looks balanced and grown-up. Proportions matter more than age.
Hosting a dinner party tonight. Went with a backless jumpsuit in deep navy and flat sandals so I can run between kitchen and table. Gold earrings and a sleek low bun to finish it off.
Our first snow of the season! The kids built a snowman while I tried my new long down coat. It covers my knees, has a two-way zip and deep pockets. I'm finally warm while waiting at the bus stop.
OOTD: camel coat, grey knit, straight jeans. 8°C and windy so the scarf stayed on all day.
Rain all morning, so trench and rubber boots it is.
Finally warm enough for the linen shirt!
Hot weather uniform: white linen trousers, a loose tank and flat thong sandals. Nothing sticks to you.
Nude heels with a navy dress is my go-to for office days that end with dinner plans.
Feeling a bit sexy in this black slip dress tonight. Layered a cropped cardigan over it because the evening got chilly.
Is a skinny jean still okay with chunky boots or should I switch to straight leg?
Tight white tee, high-waisted jeans, big black bag. Simple and it works every time.
Beach day! Striped bikini, oversized linen shirt as a cover-up and a straw hat. 31°C and not a cloud.
Those killer heels deserve a standing ovation. Where did you find them?
You look drop-dead gorgeous in that emerald gown 😍
Tops and bottoms in matching sage green. Co-ord sets save me so much time in the morning.
Cocktail dress in peacock blue for my cousin's engagement party. Kept the jewellery minimal.
A pop of colour on a grey day: mustard beanie with my charcoal coat.
These butt-lifting jeans are honestly the most comfortable denim I own. High rise, lots of stretch.
Swapped my screw-back earrings for little hoops so I could sleep in them on the overnight train.
Fanny pack worn crossbody for the farmers market. Hands free for coffee and peaches.
Humid day tip: tie up your hair in a low bun and pick a breathable cotton dress.
Tried Lolita fashion for the first time at a convention. Petticoat, lace collar, and a pastel pink rosette on the headpiece.
